checker: supports-holdings-doctrine (mechanical textual entailment only; no estate re-read, no byte-check)
standard: Quote as written must entail the claim as written. Paraphrase and within-document terminology mapping are tolerated; any substantive assertion in the claim that the quote does not entail fails the row.
quote_note: Row 1 quote contains one em-dash in the source (after 'deliberately'); it is rendered as a plain hyphen here per the seat no-em-dash law. Tier-2 must byte-check quotes against the estate source document, not against this file.

rows.claim: A holdings audit that checks only claims-to-disk cannot see an orphan, and an orphan is exactly the artifact that looks like a holding and cannot be explained; holdings are audited claims-to-disk AND disk-to-receipts.
rows.quote:
Checked in *both*
  directions deliberately - a ledger-only audit cannot see an orphan, and an orphan is exactly
  the artefact that looks like a holding and cannot be explained.
rows.reason: The quote carries every substantive part of the claim. 'a ledger-only audit cannot see an orphan' matches 'checks only claims-to-disk cannot see an orphan' (the ledger is the claims ledger in a holdings audit); 'an orphan is exactly the artefact that looks like a holding and cannot be explained' is near-verbatim (artefact/artifact spelling only); and 'Checked in both directions deliberately' asserts exactly the bidirectional audit the claim states as 'claims-to-disk AND disk-to-receipts', the second direction being the complement of the ledger-only check the quote itself rules out as insufficient.

rows.claim: A holding is deleted only when it is unclaimed by every ledger AND byte-identical to a claimed file; either condition alone and it stays, because a dedupe false positive is more dangerous than no dedupe.
rows.quote:
delete only a file that is **unclaimed AND byte-identical
to a claimed file**; both conditions or it stays.
rows.reason: The quote entails the deletion rule itself: 'delete only a file that is unclaimed AND byte-identical to a claimed file; both conditions or it stays' covers 'unclaimed by every ledger AND byte-identical to a claimed file' and 'either condition alone and it stays'. But the claim's appended rationale, 'because a dedupe false positive is more dangerous than no dedupe', appears nowhere in the quote and is not derivable from it; the quote states the rule but gives no reason for it. A quote covering only part of the claim does not entail the claim.

rows.claim: A fetched source is a live promise, not a holding; a row graduates to PULLED only when the fetched document's own text confirms the claim, because 69 of 73 title pairs were wrong and 46 Gutenberg transcripts were unrelated books.
rows.quote:
So a row moves to PULLED only
when the fetched document's own text confirms the claim:
rows.reason: The quote entails only the middle clause, near-verbatim ('a row moves to PULLED only when the fetched document's own text confirms the claim'). Two substantive parts are absent from the quote as written: the opening doctrine 'a fetched source is a live promise, not a holding', and the stated evidence 'because 69 of 73 title pairs were wrong and 46 Gutenberg transcripts were unrelated books' (the quote ends at the colon before any numbers appear). Partial entailment, so no.

rows.claim: An instrument reporting a confident zero over a corpus its match key cannot see (arXiv-token matching against non-arXiv holdings) is answering a question about someone else's corpus; every zero report must name its match key and corpus scope.
rows.quote:
It is you answering a question about a corpus that is not ours
and reporting a confident count for it.
rows.reason: The quote supports only the core metaphor: 'It is you answering a question about a corpus that is not ours and reporting a confident count for it.' Three parts of the claim are not in the quote: the zero specificity (the quote says 'count', never 'zero'), the instrument framing 'a corpus its match key cannot see (arXiv-token matching against non-arXiv holdings)' (the quote says only 'a corpus that is not ours', with no match key and no arXiv-token detail), and the prescription 'every zero report must name its match key and corpus scope'. Partial entailment, so no.

rows.claim: Bulk-pulling primaries with no live claim attaches proof to nothing; pulls happen at point-of-claim under the no-fabrication law, and metadata-only backfill is NAMED+RESOLVED, never PULLED+HASHED.
rows.quote:
Bulk-pulling 198 primary PDFs attaches proof to no live claim; the fleet's
no-fabrication law (2026-09-19) already governs primary pulls at point-of-claim.
rows.reason: The quote entails two of the three parts: 'Bulk-pulling 198 primary PDFs attaches proof to no live claim' supports 'bulk-pulling primaries with no live claim attaches proof to nothing', and 'the fleet's no-fabrication law (2026-09-19) already governs primary pulls at point-of-claim' supports 'pulls happen at point-of-claim under the no-fabrication law'. The third part, 'metadata-only backfill is NAMED+RESOLVED, never PULLED+HASHED', appears nowhere in the quote. Partial entailment, so no.
